reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a piecewise-constant, quasi-periodic sawtooth-like waveform with a robust period of ~98 points (1 cycle per 98 points), as confirmed by the reference_cycle_plan and estimated_period. Each full cycle consists of a slow linear descent (~−0.00058 to −0.00174 per point) from a plateau near +0.5–0.75, followed by a sharp drop (~−1.25 to −1.35) over ~5–10 points, then a flat or slightly rising plateau near −1.25 to −1.35 for ~10–15 points, and finally a rapid ascent back to the upper plateau over ~10–15 points. Amplitude (90th percentile) is stable at ~2.0–2.2 robust standard deviations; median is consistently 0.0, MAD ≈0.674–0.675. Peaks are broad plateaus (not sharp spikes); troughs are flat-bottomed minima. Noise is negligible—values are quantized to a coarse grid (steps of ~0.125–0.25), indicating discretization or heavy smoothing. Stability is high across candidates: all show identical motif structure, minor slope variations (<0.002/point), and no drift beyond expected within-cycle trends. Acceptable variation includes slight differences in plateau duration, exact descent/ascent steepness, and minor curvature (e.g., candidate 2 shows slight convexity in ascent), but core morphology—three-phase descent–drop–rise—is invariant.

No anomalies; best for assessing long-term stability.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer candidate 3 (5P) for queries spanning >3 cycles due to its long-context stability; use candidate 0 (1P) for short queries or when precise single-cycle alignment is needed; candidates 1 and 2 are interchangeable for 2–3 cycle queries, but choose candidate 1 if strict linearity is expected, candidate 2 if slight convex ascent is observed. When query shows curvature in rise, match to candidate 2; if perfectly linear, match to candidate 0 or 3.
